newsitem.title: JAPAN: US, Japan to hold air talks March 4-6 in Washington.
newsitem.headline: US, Japan to hold air talks March 4-6 in Washington.

text.p: The United States and Japan will hold talks on their dispute over aircraft landing rights from March 4-6 in Washington, Japan's Transport Ministry said on Tuesday.

A ministry spokesman said Hiromichi Toya, transport vice minister for international affairs, would represent Japan and Alan Larson, assistant secretary of state for business and economic affairs, would represent the United States.

The two countries held "exploratory" talks in Tokyo in January after formal discussions broke down in August. Japanese officials have said the atmosphere had greatly improved since last year and both sides are looking for a compromise.
The United States has called for "open skies" -- the lifting of most government regulations in air services -- while Japan asserts that imbalances in the existing bilateral treaty must be addressed.
